title: A loop that stops one element early
summary: Learn why a loop using `i < marks.length - 1` skips the last array element, and how to trace and fix it.
objectives: Explain why `i < marks.length - 1` skips the last array element.
Trace a `for` loop one pass at a time and identify when it stops.
Fix a loop so it visits every element in an array.
Recognize the same early-stop bug in other loops.

blocks.text: This is the pattern Code Coach flags. The loop adds `marks[0]` and `marks[1]`, but it never adds `marks[2]`. The array has three marks, so the total should include all three.

blocks.title: This usually compiles
blocks.text: Java accepts this code. The mistake is in what happens when the program runs: the loop stops before it reaches the last mark. It does not normally cause a crash or a compiler warning.

An array's `length` is the number of values in it. Here, `marks.length` is `3`. The valid indices are `0`, `1` and `2`. But subtracting `1` makes the loop condition `i < 2`. That condition allows `i` to be `0` and `1`, then stops before `i` can be `2`.

blocks.caption: `int[] marks = {60, 72, 85};`
blocks.name: marks
blocks.note: The highlighted box is the skipped last mark, at `marks[2]`. The length is `3`, but `3` is not an index of a box.

blocks.caption: The early-stop loop's decision
blocks.mermaid:
flowchart TD
  A([Start at i = 0]) --> B{i < marks.length - 1?}
  B -- yes --> C[Add marks at i to total]
  C --> D[Increase i by 1]
  D --> B
  B -- no --> E([Leave the loop])

blocks.title: Keep the two numbers separate
blocks.text: The last index is `length - 1`. But when a loop starts at `0` and should visit every array element, use `i < length`. The condition stops at the length, after it has already allowed the last index.

sections.title: Trace it, one pass at a time

blocks.text: A trace is a written record of what a program does. Check the condition before each pass, then record the change made by the body and update. Here, `marks.length - 1` is `2`.

blocks.caption: Tracing `for (int i = 0; i < marks.length - 1; i++)`
rows: The loop stops. `marks[2]`, which is `85`, is not added.

blocks.text: The loop updates `i` after the second pass, so `i` becomes `2`. It checks `2 < 2`, gets `false`, and stops. The fix is to use `i < marks.length`. Then the check at `i = 2` is `2 < 3`, which is `true`.
Both examples show the same bug as the flagged code. Compare what the program prints with the result after changing the loop condition.

bad.title: Wrong total: the last mark is skipped

good.title: Correct total: all marks are added

blocks.note: The bad program compiles and prints `132`, because it adds `60 + 72`. The good program changes the condition to `i < marks.length`, so it also adds `85` and prints `217`.

bad.title: Wrong count: the last mark is not checked

good.title: Correct count: every mark is checked

blocks.note: The bad program checks `60` and `72`, so it counts one mark at least `70`. It never checks `85`. With the corrected condition, it checks all three marks and prints `2`.

blocks.text: The exact flagged pattern is `i < marks.length - 1`. The same early stop can appear with another array name or inside a different task. It can quietly give a wrong answer while the program runs normally.

bad.title: Search skips the final value

good.title: Search checks every value

blocks.note: If `target` is in the last box, the bad loop never finds it. The loop condition should allow the index `values.length - 1`.

bad.title: Copy loop leaves the last box alone

good.title: Copy loop visits every box

blocks.note: The bad version copies every box except the last one. Remember the original pattern: subtracting `1` from the loop limit is what makes it stop early.

blocks.title: Do not subtract the last index from the limit
blocks.text: For a loop starting at `0`, the last valid index is `array.length - 1`, but the loop condition should be `i < array.length`. That condition visits the last index and stops before trying to use index `array.length`.

blocks.question: With `marks.length` equal to `3`, which indices does this loop visit?
blocks.explanation: `marks.length - 1` is `2`, so the condition is `i < 2`. The loop visits `0` and `1`, then stops before `2`.

blocks.question: Which condition visits every element in an array named `items` when the loop starts at `0`?
blocks.explanation: The condition `i < items.length` allows the loop to reach the last valid index, `items.length - 1`, and stops when `i` reaches the length.

blocks.question: The loop adds `marks[0]` and `marks[1]` from `{60, 72, 85}` using the flagged pattern. What total does it print?
blocks.explanation: The flagged condition stops before the last mark. It adds `60` and `72`, which gives `132`. This loop compiles and runs; it simply prints the wrong total.

items: The flagged pattern `i < marks.length - 1` stops before the last element.
Array indices start at `0`; an array of length `3` has indices `0`, `1` and `2`.
For a loop starting at `0` that should visit every array element, use `i < array.length`.
Trace the condition after the final intended pass. If it stops while `i` is still the last index, the loop is too short.
This mistake usually compiles and runs without a crash, but it can produce a wrong answer.
